in_hebrew.name: נְבִי
in_hebrew.long_meaning: בֶּן נְבִי - נְבִי - נָבִי - נְבִי - (בֶּן - 'son of') - (נְבִי - ' Neviah', a biblical name mentioned in Ezra 2:55, Nehemiah 7:58, 1 Chronicles 4:34, and other places.) - (in biblical Hebrew, the name means 'gift of God' or 'God is my gift') - in Christian tradition, Nevio is an uncommon name, but it has been used as a variant of Nebio or Nevia, which is associated with the biblical figure of Nebuzaradan, a Babylonian general who served under Nebuchadnezzar II.

in_greek.name: Νεβίων
in_greek.long_meaning: υἱός Νεβίου - Νεβίων - Νεβίου - (υἱός - 'son of') - (Νεβίων - 'Nevion', a Greek variant of Nevio) - (in early Christian tradition, the name Nevio was used as a translation of the Hebrew name Neviah, meaning 'gift of God' or 'God is my gift') - in New Testament times, Nevio is not directly mentioned as a biblical name, but it may have been used as an epithet or a nickname for someone known for their piety or spiritual gifts.

in_latin.name: Nevius
in_latin.long_meaning: filius Nebii - Nebius - (filius - 'son of') - (Nebius - 'Nevius', a Latin name derived from the Hebrew name Neviah, meaning 'gift of God' or 'God is my gift') - in early Christian tradition, Nevio was used as a name for someone who received a spiritual gift or was known for their piety - in Latin Christian culture, Nevio was used as a variant of the more common name Nebius.
